newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander says S&P outlook move "normal".
newsitem.headline: Santander says S&P outlook move "normal".

text.p: Spain's Banco Santander said on Wednesday the decision of Standard & Poor's rating agency to change the outlook for the group to negative from stable was "normal" following heavy investment abroad.

"We regard this decision by S&P as normal in light of the heavy investment we've made but in no way negative for the bank because the rating agency recognised that the bank has the necessary expertise to succeed in Latin America," a bank spokesman told Reuters.
Earlier, S&P said it had revised Santander's outlook to negative after its latest acquisition of a 35 percent stake in Argentinian bank Banco Rio de la Plata.
"S&Ps recognition of Santander's management skills was also a factor in the bank's outlook having been restored to stable after being modified with the purchase of Banesto in 1994.
"We are confident again our investment in a high-profit bank in Argentina will demonstrate this management expertise again," the spokesman said.
S&P maintained Santander's long-term and short-term debt ratings at AA minus and A-1 plus respectively.
